summary: Today’s pulse tracks Parents sue to stop Washington state trans sports ban that could require ‘invasive’ genital exams, Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House minority leader after midterm defeats, and Republicans elect Ohio congressman Jim Jordan as House minority leader – US politics live. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are jordan, house, and republicans. In the background, UK counter-terrorism police arrest member of US army with alleged links to Russia and Trump’s FCC nominee avoids questions from Democrats on Carr’s ‘censorship agenda’ keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Parents sue to stop Washington state trans sports ban that could require ‘invasive’ genital exams
headlines.description: Voters adopted extreme policy requiring medical sex verification for all girls who want to play team sports Parents of student athletes in Washington state have sued to block a ballot initiative banning transgender girls from women’s sports teams, calling the measure discriminatory and warning it would lead to “invasive” genital examinations for female athletes. Last week, voters in the solidly Democratic state passed Initiative 638 , a major setback for LGBTQ+ rights amid the “blue wave” of the US midterm elections. Nebraska, Colorado and Arizona adopted similar anti-trans sports bans, though advocates say Washington state’s policy is particularly extreme due to its medical sex verification requirement for all girls who want to play team sports.

headlines.title: Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House minority leader after midterm defeats
headlines.description: As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress, Republicans pick Jordan for last two years of Trump’s presidency Republican lawmakers have elected Jim Jordan, veteran congressman and Trump loyalist, as their leader in the House of Representatives following resounding losses in last week’s US midterm elections. As Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers of US Congress in January, Republicans backed Jordan to lead them in the House for the last two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.

headlines.title: Republicans elect Ohio congressman Jim Jordan as House minority leader – US politics live
headlines.description: Hardline conservative Jordan beat Steve Scalise by a vote of 106-73 Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House minority leader after party’s midterm defeats “As for the articles themselves, Iran, the cartels, Maduro, Yemen, everyone was a lawful operation ordered by the commander-in-chief, then ordered by myself, notified to Congress and executed by American warriors who did their jobs,” he said. “We destroyed terror regimes’ capabilities. We sank the boats carrying poison into our communities. We put a narco dictator in handcuffs. These are not high crimes. This is the job, and it’s the job well done.”

headlines.title: UK counter-terrorism police arrest member of US army with alleged links to Russia
headlines.description: Man, 41, arrested as part of an investigation by British police working with US authorities, US military and FBI A member of the US army with alleged links to Russia has been arrested by British counter-terrorism police. The man, 41, was arrested as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing, working closely with US authorities, the US military and the FBI, Counter Terrorism Policing London said.

headlines.title: Trump’s FCC nominee avoids questions from Democrats on Carr’s ‘censorship agenda’
headlines.description: Senators pressured Danielle Thumann, senior counsel to FCC chair Brendan Carr, to speak about agency’s actions toward ABC and Jimmy Kimmel During a contentious Tuesday hearing on her nomination by Donald Trump to serve as a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) commissioner, Senate Democrats hammered Danielle Thumann about recent actions taken by the Brendan Carr-led regulator that have been criticized as hostile to press freedom. Thumann, who serves as senior counsel to Carr, is expected to be approved as commissioner, with Republicans in charge of the US Senate and House. But Ben Ray Luján, a senator of New Mexico, assured her that the commission’s actions will be under close scrutiny when Democrats take charge of the chamber in January.

headlines.title: Falkland Islanders face ‘devastating consequences’ if Argentina blocks oil project, says UK
headlines.description: Countries clash over Sea Lion project as Hamburg tribunal risks deepening sovereignty dispute The people of the Falkland Islands face “devastating consequences” if Argentina is successful in blocking development of its offshore oilfield, the attorney general for England and Wales has told an international tribunal. Ellie Reeves, representing the British government at a hearing of the international tribunal for the law of the sea (Itlos), said billions of pounds vital to the future of the British overseas territory would be lost.

headlinePool.title: Testing the new generation of AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones
headlinePool.description: Drone makers are testing new, big drones that can deliver water or fire retardant with AI assistance. Aspen, Colorado is the first place trying them out. Cool and expensive? Yes. Effective? TBD.

headlinePool.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running
headlinePool.description: The U.S. has skipped a key U.N. human rights review for the second year running. Rights groups warn the absence risks undermining global accountability.

headlinePool.title: House Republicans urge DoJ to further investigate ‘key witnesses’ in Epstein case
headlinePool.description: Republicans on House panel criticize US government’s investigation into Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell Republicans on the House oversight committee released a report on Tuesday criticizing the federal government’s handling of the investigations into Jeffrey Epstein and his associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, and called on the Department of Justice to interview “key witnesses, investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity, and ensure survivors have access to their records”. “The federal government has failed the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s horrific crimes for decades,” James Comer, the Republican congressman who chairs the committee, said in a statement .

headlinePool.title: Meet the Peaky Blinders, Ukraine's drone unit protecting a devastated front-line city
headlinePool.description: Slovyansk continues to be bombarded by Russian forces, making it almost uninhabitable with less than 10% of it's pre-war population remaining.

headlinePool.title: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
headlinePool.description: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.

headlinePool.title: Judge who sentenced Russell Brand praised for dispelling rape myths
headlinePool.description: Criminal Bar Association and campaigners hail Mr Justice Bennathan for delivering remarks with ‘piercing clarity’ The judge who sentenced Russell Brand has been praised for dispelling rape myths with “piercing clarity”. Mr Justice Bennathan’s sentencing remarks were particularly welcomed given that rape myths had played a part in the trial. He was also lauded for calling out “enablers” who witnessed sexual assaults by the comedian.

headlinePool.title: Woman jailed for posing as man to dupe partner into sex found guilty of similar deception
headlinePool.description: Jury finds Blade Silvano, who presented herself as a male army veteran, guilty of six counts of sexual assault A woman serving a prison sentence for sexual assault after pretending to be a man and duping a woman into a physical relationship has been found guilty of tricking another woman into a similar abusive partnership. In both cases, Blade Silvano, 44, met the women on an online dating site and falsely claimed she was a man who had served in the armed forces before meeting them in person and sexually assaulting them. Information and support for anyone affected by rape or sexual abuse issues is available from the following organisations. In the UK, Rape Crisis offers support on 0808 500 2222 in England and Wales, 0808 801 0302 in Scotland , or 0800 0246 991 in Northern Ireland . In the US, Rainn offers support on 800-656-4673. In Australia, support is available at 1800Respect (1800 737 732). Other international helplines can be found at ibiblio.org/rcip/internl.html

headlinePool.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
headlinePool.description: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.

headlinePool.title: Why are these purple flowers shutting down streets in Sydney?
headlinePool.description: Jacaranda trees typically flower for six weeks every spring, drawing visitors to Australia from across the globe.
